GCSE chem revision, can you check my answers? Question was "Describe how the model of the atom has changed over time" (6 marks)

My answer:
Dalton (1803) said atoms were solid spheres that couldnt be divided. Then JJ Thomson discovered the electron in 1897 and came up with the plum pudding model, a ball of positive charge with electrons stuck in it. Rutherford, Geiger and Marsden did the gold foil experiment in 1909 and most alpha particles went straight through but a few bounced back, so the mass and positive charge must be in a tiny nucleus. Then Bohr said electrons orbit at fixed distances (shells). Then Chadwick found the neutron in 1932.

Also two calc ones:
(a) "A sample of magnesium has a mass of 6.0 g. Calculate the number of moles. Ar of Mg = 24." I put 0.25 mol.
(b) "How many atoms is that?" I put 0.25 x 6.02 x 10^23 = 1.505 x 10^23. Is that ok to 3 sig figs or should it be 1.51 x 10^23?

∫ x² e^(3x) dx

u = x², dv = e^(3x) dx → du = 2x dx, v = (1/3)e^(3x)

second round: u = 2x/3, dv = e^(3x) dx → du = (2/3) dx, v = (1/3)e^(3x)
